jobs.aboutRole:
The Quality Control Intern – Hardware is the checkpoint every recording rig passes through, in both directions. When rigs return from the field, you inspect their condition, run a functional check, and capture a short test recording that you review to confirm the cameras, footage, audio, and storage are all working. Before any rig goes back out, you give the final sign-off that it is field-ready.
This is a small role with an outsized impact: a rig that leaves your desk in a bad state means a Field Officer travels to a business, records for hours, and returns with unusable or missing data — a full day lost, and sometimes a burned business relationship. Your job is to make sure that never happens. Precision, consistency, and discipline are the whole game here.

You are the last line of defense on rig quality before it reaches a business.

Only mark a rig "field-ready" once every check passes

Quarantine any rig that fails QC so it cannot accidentally go to field
Log the exact fault clearly (which component, what's wrong) and escalate hardware faults to the Hardware/IT team
Follow up so repaired rigs are re-checked before they re-enter circulation
Maintain clean, complete QC records in Google Sheets — every rig, every check, pass/fail, date/time, and reason

AI has made it incredibly easy to produce content. There are more articles, posts, emails, videos, and opinions competing for people's attention every day.
We think this makes genuinely good content more valuable.
We're looking for a Content Marketing Intern who wants to become exceptionally good at understanding an audience, finding ideas worth talking about, and turning those ideas into work people actually want to read, watch, save, share, and come back to.
At Prodigal, good content starts with understanding.
You'll learn how financial institutions operate, how their teams work, what their customers experience, what executives care about, where processes break, and how AI is changing the industry. We go unusually deep into these details. We obsess over the people, processes, regulations, and edge cases that shape how this industry actually works.
That level of understanding should show up in everything we publish.
